Article Title: Bangladesh PM likely to visit India as Dhaka presses for Sheikh Hasina's extradition
Article Text:
Tarique Rahman likely to visit India

Bangladesh Prime Minister Tarique Rahman’s proposed visit to India has not yet been finalised, with the timing dependent on his “schedule” and the “progress” of ongoing bilateral discussions."The government is positive about visits to all countries. But it will depend on the PM's schedule and on how far discussions between the two countries progress," state minister for foreign affairs Shama Obaed Islam said."The government is busy, and so is the prime minister. If everything fits together, of course there will be a visit to India, a visit to Japan; all the visits will happen," she said, referring to ongoing domestic programmes and upcoming constitutional activities.In April, Bangladesh foreign minister Khalilur Rahman visited India as part of efforts to mend strained bilateral ties following more than 18 months of heightened diplomatic tensions.Bangladesh has also sought the extradition of former prime minister Sheikh Hasina.External affairs ministry spokesperson Randhir Jaiswal said on Tuesday that India has extended two separate invitations to Bangladesh Prime Minister Tarique Rahman — one for a bilateral visit and another to attend the outreach session of the Brics Summit in New Delhi in September."Brics is still a long way off. A lot can happen in a month,” Shama said.Asked whether Rahman’s visit to India could help ease tensions, Shama said direct communication between the leaders of the two governments could provide an opportunity to discuss and resolve outstanding issues."Whenever the heads of two countries talk, there is a chance of resolving many problems. That opportunity is there; it remains," she said.Relations between India and Bangladesh deteriorated sharply after the interim government led by Muhammad Yunus came to power following the fall of Sheikh Hasina’s government in August 2024.Efforts to stabilise ties gained momentum after Lok Sabha Speaker Om Birla, accompanied by foreign secretary Vikram Misri, represented India at Tarique Rahman’s swearing-in ceremony in Dhaka on February 17.Rahman assumed office as prime minister after his party secured a landslide victory in the parliamentary elections.Bangladesh’s current government, led by Rahman’s Bangladesh Nationalist Party, has maintained that Sheikh Hasina must surrender and face the law if she returns to the country.Hasina recently addressed an audio-only virtual press conference from New Delhi, her first public media interaction since fleeing to India on August 5, 2024, amid mass protests.During the virtual press conference, Hasina said she was determined to return to Bangladesh in December to put the country on the "right track" by restoring democracy, despite facing the possibility of imprisonment or a death sentence.India distanced itself from Hasina’s media interaction, clarifying that it had neither played a role in organising the event nor endorsed her remarks concerning the Bangladesh government.
Article Summary: Bangladesh Prime Minister Tarique Rahman’s proposed visit to India has not yet been finalised, with the timing dependent on his “schedule” and the “progress” of ongoing bilateral discussions. Bangladesh foreign minister Khalilur Rahman visited India in April as part of efforts to mend strained bilateral ties.

Article Title: 'A moment that tore apart several lives': PM Modi on Partition Horrors Remembrance Day
Article Text:
Partition triggered one of the largest mass migrations in history, affecting an estimated 20 million people.

NEW DELHI: A day ahead of Independence Day , Prime Minister Narendra Modi on Friday paid tribute to those affected by the Partition of India, remembering their courage and resilience on Partition Horrors Remembrance Day.He described the day as an occasion to remember those whose lives were upended by Partition, which "tore apart several lives, uprooted families and caused immense suffering."“Today we mark Partition Horrors Remembrance Day. We recall the courage of all those who were impacted by Partition. It was a moment in history that tore apart several lives... families were uprooted, loved ones were lost, and immense suffering was endured,” PM Modi wrote in a post on X.The prime minister said that despite the hardships, those affected rebuilt their lives from scratch, overcame adversity and made significant contributions to the country's progress.“Their life journeys remind us of the strength of the human spirit. May this day deepen our resolve to preserve harmony and brotherhood in our nation and collectively work towards building a Viksit Bharat,” he added.India has observed Partition Horrors Remembrance Day on August 14 since 2021 to honour those who lost their lives or were displaced during the Partition of 1947.India gained independence from British rule on August 15, 1947. However, the birth of two new nations - India and Pakistan - was accompanied by the violent Partition, which left deep and lasting scars on millions of people.Partition triggered one of the largest mass migrations in history, affecting an estimated 20 million people. Millions were forced to leave their ancestral homes, villages, towns and cities and begin new lives as refugees.The upheaval was accompanied by widespread communal violence and the loss of countless lives, leaving a lasting impact on generations that followed.
Article Summary: PM Narendra Modi pays tribute to those affected by the Partition of India. Partition triggered one of the largest mass migrations in history, affecting an estimated 20 million people. India has observed Partition Horrors Remembrance Day on August 14 since 2021.

NEW DELHI: Air India group has from Thursday started 'mandatory substance screening' for all pilots following the Phuket-Delhi flight serious incident. The move comes to “protect and sustain” the trust AI had earned over the decades that has been shaken by the pilot-in-command of the Phuket flight testing positive for marijuana. We nevertheless now feel it is important to go further.Accordingly we have decided to undertake a full screening of all group pilots for any substances or medications that are not permitted under prevailing regulations. This testing is mandatory and will start today, 13 August 2026.”“It will be conducted concurrently with training at the Gurugram Academy, post flight at our Flight Briefing Centres / Air India Offices, or at locations provided by your respective bases. This initiative, which goes beyond regulatory requirements, reflects our determination to uphold the highest standards of safety and professionalism, and to provide reassurance to our passengers, stakeholders and the community at large. Preparing creators for the future

As India's creator economy continues to redefine entertainment, entrepreneurship and storytelling, Uttar Pradesh is emerging as one of the country's fastest-growing hubs for digital innovation. With increasing internet penetration, a thriving startup ecosystem and the rapid rise of creators from Tier 2 and Tier 3 cities, the state is playing a pivotal role in shaping India's digital future.Celebrating this transformation, the inaugural edition Times of India’s UP Creators Summit & Awards will bring together some of the state's most influential content creators, industry leaders, brands and digital innovators for a 2-day mega showcase of recognition, insightful conversations and future-focused learning.To be held on August 19 and 20 in Varanasi, the spiritual and cultural heart of Uttar Pradesh, the event will bring together the state’s rich heritage and its new-age digital voices, showcasing how creators are shaping the narrative of a new Uttar Pradesh. The first day, August 19, will feature insightful masterclasses, panel discussions and fireside chats, while August 20 will culminate in the grand UP Creators Awards, celebrating the state’s most impactful digital creators.At the heart of the event are the Creators Awards, which will honour creators who are making a meaningful impact across diverse genres, including education, technology, finance, food, travel, lifestyle, comedy, fashion, gaming, social impact and more. These creators are not only building communities online but are also amplifying local stories, inspiring millions and showcasing Uttar Pradesh's talent on the national and global stage. The awards celebrate creators who are redefining digital influence while contributing to the state's growing reputation as a powerhouse of innovation and creativity.Beyond the awards, the summit will serve as a platform for thought-provoking discussions on the opportunities and challenges shaping the creator ecosystem.Panel discussions will explore how the creator economy is expanding beyond metropolitan cities into Tier 2 and Tier 3 India, the growing influence of creators in rebranding Uttar Pradesh, and the role of digital storytellers in building the narrative of a new Uttar Pradesh. The event will also feature engaging fireside chats on themes such as "Storytellers of a New Bharat" and "Beyond Followers", examining how creators are moving beyond metrics to create meaningful impact, influence culture and build sustainable careers.As artificial intelligence reshapes the content landscape, the summit will host a dedicated AI Masterclass on future-proofing content creation. The session will provide practical insights into how creators can leverage AI-powered tools to enhance creativity, improve productivity and stay ahead in an increasingly competitive digital ecosystem.Bringing together creators, policymakers, industry experts and ecosystem enablers, the UP Creators Summit & Awards aims to celebrate the diverse voices driving India's digital revolution while highlighting Uttar Pradesh's emergence as one of the country's most exciting creator hubs. Article Title: Use medical tourists' money to treat poor Indians: Panel
Article Text:

NEW DELHI: Revenue earned from foreign patients and affluent Indians should help fund treatment for poorer patients, a Parliamentary Standing Committee on Health and Family Welfare has recommended, proposing that corporate hospitals adopt a cross-subsidisation model to make advanced healthcare more affordable.The panel said hospitals that benefit from government concessions such as subsidised land, tax incentives and 100% foreign direct investment (FDI) should earmark part of the revenue generated from medical tourism and high-paying patients to provide advanced tertiary care to economically weaker Indians.The recommendation is part of the committee's report on the affordability and accessibility of healthcare, which noted that India's corporate hospital sector has recorded strong growth driven by high-value procedures, rising medical tourism and increasing revenue per occupied bed. While acknowledging India's emergence as a global healthcare destination, the panel said the benefits of this growth must also reach patients who cannot afford expensive treatment.Observing that private health insurance penetration in India remains low and out-of-pocket expenditure continues to push many families into financial distress, the committee said a structured cross-subsidy mechanism could improve access to life-saving tertiary care for poorer patients.It said hospitals receiving government support should share part of the gains from medical tourism and premium-paying patients with economically weaker sections.The panel also recommended that corporate hospitals reserve a defined quota of beds under government-funded health insurance schemes such as Ayushman Bharat PM-JAY at standard package rates to ensure that beneficiaries have access to advanced treatment at leading private hospitals.To address the uneven distribution of healthcare infrastructure, the committee proposed linking government incentives, including subsidised land, tax benefits and FDI facilitation, to investment in tier-2, tier-3 and rural areas. It also recommended expanding public-private partnerships and extending financial and technology support to smaller hospitals in underserved regions.The recommendations form part of a broader roadmap to make healthcare more affordable. The committee has also proposed capping private hospital room rents in major metropolitan cities at the average tariff of nearby three-star hotels, standardising treatment package rates, improving price transparency and expanding government health spending to reduce out-of-pocket expenditure.
Article Summary: Hospitals receiving government support should share part of the gains from medical tourism and premium-paying patients with economically weaker sections. The panel also recommended that corporate hospitals reserve a defined quota of beds under government-funded health insurance schemes such as Ayushman Bharat PM-JAY.

Article Title: Phuket plunge: Airbus sends initial report to AI, seeks maintenance details
Article Text:
Airbus has asked Air In- dia to carry out multiple tests and share the aircraft’s recent maintenance activi- ties as it continues its event assessment

NEW DELHI: “The elevators (control up and down movement of aircraft) and ailerons (controls left and right movement) surfaces were lost for around four seconds.” Airbus, in its initial assessment of the A320 flying from Phuket to Delhi on Aug 4, said the aircraft experienced a sudden loss in altitude that left 24 injured.“Based on analysis of the DFDR (digital flight data recorder),” Airbus found that within seven seconds between 9:32:44 am and 9:32:51 am, there was a loss of hydraulics systems — pressurised fluids which enable flight controls to move. At this point, the autopilot was disconnected and the aircraft’s nose went up (increase in pitch). All timings are in IST.The Airbus preliminary communication sent to AI on Aug 10 says “at (9:32:46 am) auto pilot 2 was disconnected, and full nose down (pitch down) input began being applied on first officer side with no direct response from the flight control surfaces” due to the loss of hydraulics. Five seconds later, a single hydraulic system was recovered and a few seconds later the remaining two systems were back, leading to recovery of normal flight control.Airbus has asked Air India to carry out multiple tests and share the aircraft’s recent maintenance activities as it continues its event assessment. “Since load exceedances were detected during the sudden altitude change, (maintenance) inspections must be performed.Please provide the inspection results once they are completed. Please provide more detailed pilot reports from the reported event clarifying what it is observed during the event,” the communication says.“...this event requires an analysis considering both aircraft systems and structural integrity, as airframe may have been affected by the movement,” it adds.While probe is on by Airbus and France’s accident investigator under the ambit of India’s Aircraft Accident Investigation Bureau, several pilots are questioning why Air India decided to fly the aircraft all the way to Delhi after it had recovered from the technical events.
Article Summary: Airbus has asked Air India to carry out multiple tests and share the aircraft’s recent maintenance activities. Airbus, in its initial assessment of the A320 flying from Phuket to Delhi on Aug 4, said the aircraft experienced a sudden loss in altitude that left 24 injured.

Article Title: BCI bars Nalsar students over CJI Surya Kant protest, retracts
Article Text:

NEW DELHI: If the directive was unusual, the withdrawal was dramatic.Bar Council of India (BCI) on Thursday took back its communication — hours after issuing it — to Hyderabad-based Nalsar University of Law that said those who organised opposition to the invitation to CJI Surya Kant for the institute’s convocation would not be enrolled as advocates.In a fresh communication late evening, BCI chairperson Manan Kumar Mishra said the council had “thoroughly discussed and deliberated” on his earlier letter to Nalsar’s vice-chancellor and state bar council secretaries and modified its direction.BCI — the statutory regulating body for legal education and profession — is of the unanimous view that, according to the “latest report”, vast majority of Nalsar’s 2026 graduating students were innocent and “were not inclined to take part in the move of disrespect”, he said. However, Mishra said, “It has been further reported by some reliable sources that a handful of teachers and outsiders were instrumental in instigating innocent students. ” BCI will wait for the “inquiry report” from Nalsar, he said in the fresh letter, which he posted on his X handle.SCBA president Vikas Singh reacted sharply to BCI chairperson’s earlier letter to Nalsar by condemning its ‘arbitrary’ decision to stall enrolment of law graduates from the university.Singh said the decision is illegal, disproportionate and fundamentally unsustainable. However, he said he did not support the section of students who opposed the invitation to the CJI.This story continues on page 10 in the newspaper. For your reading convenience we have added it below.Disrespectful law students are a liability, says BCI chiefIn his earlier letter to one of India’s top law schools, Mishra had sought a “factual report” about the persons instrumental in “intimidation of a constitutional functionary” by initiating, organising or mobilising the campaign against participation of CJI at the convocation ceremony.BCI chairperson had said, “Till further orders, no student of Nalsar University of Law, who has obtained law degree in the year 2026, shall be enrolled by any state bar council as an advocate.” He said a final decision on this issue would be taken on Aug 19 after receiving a report from VC.The council had requested Nalsar to differentiate between persons who have merely signed or supported the representations from those who organised or coordinated the campaign and those who proposed or mobilised an actual boycott, obstruction or disruption. “BCI does not, at this stage, record that any person stands disqualified from enrolment under Section 24A (of Advocates Act) merely on account of participation in the aforesaid representation or campaign,” Mishra had said in his first letter.TOI on Aug 10 had reported that a section of students at Nalsar had requested the university to reconsider inviting CJI Kant for its upcoming convocation taking exception to CJI’s remarks during the hearing on alleged police excesses against student protesters’ march to Parliament on July 20. The petitioner wanted the CJI-led bench to go through the video footage of police action. CJI turned down the plea saying he did not have time to watch videos.The university has not yet finalised the date of convocation, for which the CJI had been traditionally invited as the chief guest.In his first communication, the BCI chief had said, “A student of Law, having no regard or respect for the highest judicial office of the country, is not expected to be a responsible or sensible advocate, teacher or a judge. Such persons shall always be a liability on the profession. Such conduct reflects adversely upon the person’s suitability for entry into or association with the legal profession and is inconsistent with the dignity, discipline and ethical standards of the legal profession.” He said, “As per some reliable sources, there exists groupism and dirty politics among some of the academic staff and they have played a very active role in misleading, instigating and misguiding the students. This is a very serious matter. The teachers, instead of involving themselves in their teaching job, are doing nasty politics in the campus. BCI, being the regulator of Legal Education cannot be a mute spectator of such a serious situation.”“However, where material concerning the conduct of a particular applicant is under active statutory examination by the BCI and such examination may have a bearing upon regulatory considerations governing entry into the profession, completion of enrolment during pendency of such examination may create a fait accompli and render the statutory examination ineffective,” it had said asking the state bar councils to withhold registration of law graduates from Nalsar till further orders.
Article Summary: Bar Council of India (BCI) on Thursday took back its communication to Hyderabad- based Nalsar University of Law that said those who organised opposition would not be enrolled as advocates. The decision follows a campaign by the students againsts the participation of CJI Surya Kant in the convocation ceremony.

Article Title: Indian officials likely to join Taliban’s Victory Day celebrations
Article Text:
The invitation for the event has been extended by Afghanistan charge d'affaires Mufti Noor Ahmad Noor

NEW DELHI: As India and the Taliban-ruled Afghanistan further intensify their pragmatic engagement focused on trade, humanitarian aid, and regional security, the Taliban will celebrate the fifth anniversary of the Victory Day in the Afghanistan embassy here on Monday, next week. Victory Day is observed annually by the Taliban on August 15 to commemorate the group's return to Kabul in 2021, following the withdrawal of US-led NATO forces.The invitation for the event has been extended by Afghanistan charge d’affaires Mufti Noor Ahmad Noor and carries the emblem of the Islamic Emirate of Afghanistan. According to sources, who spoke on condition of anonymity, the event is not just endorsed by the Indian side but is will also see participation by senior Indian officials.India doesn’t officially recognise the Islamic Emirate, maintaining its position on that issue is in consonance with the international community, although it has allowed the Taliban to take control of the Afghan embassy. However, its position is also marked by pragmatic engagement with Taliban, leveraging its historic goodwill and development presence to protect its security and regional interests. These efforts have been further aided by the dramatic shift in the Taliban’s ties with Pakistan.India and Afghanistan continue to back each other’s sovereignty and territorial integrity with India solidly standing by Kabul in the latter’s border conflict with Pakistan. Much to Pakistan’s chagrin, the Taliban too backed India’s sovereignty over J&K in a joint statement with India last year by endorsing a mention of the union territory as located in India, while condemning the Pahalgam terrorist attack.While restoring its own embassy in Kabul last year, India had agreed to the appointment of Taliban diplomats here, allowing them to work out of the embassy even in the absence of a formal recognition for the Taliban regime. The development followed a landmark visit by Afghanistan foreign minister Amir Khan Muttaqi to India that further cemented the relationship.India’s historical and civilizational ties with Afghanistan, along with the development partnership, has witnessed more than 500 projects spread across each of the 34 provinces of the country in critical areas of power, water supply, road connectivity, healthcare, education, agriculture and capacity building.
Article Summary: The Taliban will celebrate the fifth anniversary of the Victory Day in the Afghanistan embassy here on Monday, next week. Victory Day is observed annually by the Taliban on August 15 to commemorate the group's return to Kabul in 2021, following the withdrawal of US-led NATO forces. The invitation for the event has been extended by Afghanistan charge d’affaires Mufti Noor Ahmad Noor.

Article Title: Mines, minerals bill gets nod, draws fire from Jharkhand, Kerala
Article Text:
Lok Sabha passed the bill Wednesday, while Rajya Sabha cleared it Thursday

NEW DELHI: Parliament Thu-rsday passed Mines and Minerals (Development and Regulation) Amendment Bill, 2026, which seeks to restrict states’ powers to levy taxes on mineral rights and mineral-bearing lands. Govt said the new law doesn’t seek to interfere with the autonomy of states, but aims to ensure uniform mineral rates.Lok Sabha passed the bill Wednesday, while Rajya Sabha cleared it Thursday. While no Congress MP participated in the discussion, others in the opposition, including DMK, BJD, RJD and Left parties, raised questions on whether the law would adversely impact revenues of state govts.Replying to the debate, mines minister G Kishan Reddy said Centre was seeking to regulate major minerals such as coal, limestone, iron ore, copper and manganese, while states would continue to have powers over 49 minor minerals.Reddy alleged coal blocks allocated during UPA’s tenure were a “scam” while claiming mineral allocations over the past 12 years had been transparent. He said states’ share of mineral revenue had risen from 65% in 2014-15 to 85% now, while their share of coal revenue had increased from 51% to 96%. He said Centre receives only about 11% of mineral revenue, with 88% going to states, and asserted that no state would suffer any revenue loss.Jharkhand CM Hemant Soren, however, announced a statewide agitation against the legislation, warning that “the entire nation will witness its scale” if Centre did not withdraw it. Kerala CM VD Satheesan also said his govt would oppose the new law, alleging the proposed changes would encroach upon powers of states over land. tnn
Article Summary: Parliament passed Mines and Minerals (Development and Regulation) Amendment Bill, 2026. Law seeks to restrict states’ powers to levy taxes on mineral rights and mineral-bearing lands. Article Title: 'No NALSAR 2026 graduate will be enrolled as advocate': BCI amid CJI convocation invite row
Article Text:
The decision follows a campaign by the students againsts the participation of CJI Surya Kant in the convocation ceremony.

NEW DELHI: The Bar Council of India (BCI) has directed all state bar councils to halt the enrolment of any 2026 law graduate from NALSAR University of Law, Hyderabad, as an advocate until further orders. This follows an alleged organised campaign against the participation of Chief Justice Surya Kant in the university’s convocation ceremony.The directive was issued by bar council chairman Manan Kumar Mishra, who said the Council had taken note of reports and material in the public domain regarding an organised campaign at NALSAR's convocation ceremony.The bar council has also sought an authenticated factual report from the university within three days and said the matter will be considered on August 19, after the vice-chancellor submits the report.The council has asked NALSAR to identify, on the basis of verifiable material, the persons allegedly instrumental in initiating, drafting, circulating, coordinating or mobilising the campaign. It has sought details of those involved in organising meetings, communicating with the media, administering social media or organised groups used for coordination, or proposing or mobilising any call for boycott, obstruction, disruption or organised non-participation in the convocation or any programme connected with the CJI.The bar council has also sought information on whether any student body, student bar council, students’ union or other recognised student organisation was involved in initiating, approving, coordinating or circulating the campaign. The university has also been asked to specify whether any faculty member, research scholar, alumnus or outsider participated in initiating, drafting, coordinating, advising or facilitating the campaign.In addition, the council has requested copies of relevant resolutions, minutes, agendas or other official records of meetings connected with the matter, and details of whether permission was sought or granted for any protest or organised activity and whether university rules governing student conduct or official functions were invoked.At the same time, the bar council clarified that participation in the representation or campaign would not automatically result in disqualification from enrolment. It said a distinction must be maintained between those who merely signed or supported a representation and those who organised or coordinated the campaign or proposed or mobilised an actual boycott, obstruction or disruption.The bar council said that where material concerning the conduct of a particular applicant is under statutory examination, completing enrolment during the pendency of such examination could create a fait accompli and render the examination ineffective.Accordingly, it directed that where the BCI specifically communicates the name of a person for further statutory consideration, no enrolment order should be passed in respect of that person and, if an application is already pending, the final decision should remain deferred during the inquiry.State bar councils have also been instructed to ensure that any person whose name is communicated by the bar council does not circumvent the pending examination by seeking enrolment before another state bar council. The council clarified that such communication at the preliminary stage would not itself constitute a conclusive finding of misconduct or disqualification.The bar council said any final adverse decision would be taken in accordance with the Advocates Act, 1961, the applicable rules and principles of natural justice.The communication further emphasised that legal education permits critical reasoning, debate and analysis of judicial decisions, but said there is a distinction between reasoned criticism and conduct which, if established after due examination, may involve intimidation, obstruction, organised disruption or disregard of institutional responsibilities attached to the legal profession.The communication has been issued to NALSAR University of Law as well as the secretaries of all state bar councils for necessary compliance.
Article Summary: The Bar Council of India (BCI) has directed all state bar councils to halt the enrolment of any 2026 law graduate from NALSAR University of Law, Hyderabad, as an advocate. This follows an alleged organised campaign against the participation of Chief Justice Surya Kant in the university’s convocation ceremony.

Article Title: SC slams Centre &FSSAI, says you can’t take court for a ride
Article Text:
SC was hearing a plea filed by NGO '3S and Our Health Society'

NEW DELHI: The Supreme Court Thursday slammed the Centre and the Food Safety and Standards Authority of India ( FSSAI ) for not implementing its direction on 'front-of-pack warning labels' on processed food packages and said their top priority should be the health of citizens and not the interest of MNCs.A bench of Justices J B Pardiwala and K Vinod Chandran said the court could not be taken for a ride. The bench said its Feb order was not merely a suggestion but a direction to FSSAI which had to be complied with. It said FSSAI was bowing down to the manufacturing industry and made it clear that if the food regulator didn't do it, the court would pass an order. It granted two weeks to FSSAI to reconsider its stance.In Feb, the court directed the Centre and the FSSAI to give top priority to the health concerns of citizens and not to the interests of multinational companies and asked it to implement a 'front-of-pack warning labels' system on processed food packages to ensure clear, front-facing symbols designed to instantly identify ingredients like sugar, salt and saturated fat, besides calories.It also rejected the Centre's contention that international standards could not be applied in India and asked whether India should remain underdeveloped.SC was hearing a plea filed by NGO '3S and Our Health Society'. The regulator informed SC consultations were held with all stakeholders in March, and a majority of industry organisations were opposed to the inclusion of 'warning labels' and favoured an approach intended to enable informed consumer decisions "without creating fear among consumers".The court asked govt to respond within two weeks. "We have made ourselves abundantly clear that we are concerned with the health of citizens... We still impress upon the Union of India to seriously consider the suggestion and take appropriate action."
Article Summary: SC was hearing a plea filed by NGO '3S and Our Health Society' Justices J B Pardiwala and K Vinod Chandran said the court could not be taken for a ride. The bench said its Feb order was not merely a suggestion but a direction to FSSAI.

Article Title: Air India begins dope test on all its 5,000 pilots
Article Text:
After this one-time mega exercise, AI will conduct dope tests according to regulatory requirement

NEW DELHI: Over 5,000 pilots of Air India and Air India Express have started undergoing "mandatory substance screening" from Thursday. The airline took this move to "protect and sustain" passenger trust - which had taken a hit after last June's Ahmedabad crash and was slowly being restored - but has been shaken yet again after the badly rattled Aug 4 Phuket-Delhi flight's pilot-in-command failed his dope test. After this one-time mega exercise, AI will conduct dope tests according to regulatory requirement, which as of now mandate at least 10% crew members be tested annually. DGCA is reviewing its rules and may go in for stricter consequences for those testing positive due to addiction issues and adopt a different approach for those who do so after taking medicines for pain, allergy and other issues. Pointing out that AI has over the decades "earned trust of millions of passengers and the wider community," AI senior VP (flight ops) Captain Manish Uppal wrote to all pilots Thursday: "...This trust is our most important asset, and it is vital that we do all possible to protect & sustain it."
Article Summary: Over 5,000 pilots of Air India and Air India Express have started undergoing "mandatory substance screening" from Thursday. The airline took this move to "protect and sustain" passenger trust. After this one-time mega exercise, AI will conduct dope tests according to regulatory requirement.

NEW DELHI: Red-flagging lapses in the country’s ongoing programme to increase and improve green cover, the Comptroller and Auditor General of India (CAG) has pointed out non-achievement of forest cover targets, noting that the observed increase in forest cover fell short by nearly 98% during 10 years of implementation (2015-16 to 2024-25) of the Green India Mission (GIM).Releasing the performance audit report on the Mission, CAG highlighted the wrong choice of landscape for planting trees, absence of convergence of various schemes to increase green cover, financial mismanagement, improper planning, lack of coordination and deficient monitoring behind non-achievement of the GIM’s goals.The broad objectives under the Mission were to increase forest/tree cover, improve the quality of forest/non-forest lands, improve ecosystem services, including biodiversity, hydrological services and carbon sequestration because of forest land/non-forest land, and to increase forest-based livelihood income of households living in and around forests.Underlining its key audit findings, the CAG in its report tabled in Parliament on Wednesday said, “As against the target of 1.4 million hectares (mha), improvement of forest cover quality was observed in only 0.11 mha (nearly 92% shortfall). Similarly, an increase in forest cover was observed in only 0.03 mha as against the target of 1.4 mha (nearly 98% shortfall).”It also noted that despite vulnerability being a key criterion, landscapes with low to moderate priority were selected over those more vulnerable to climate change for afforestation under the Mission.The performance audit examined the planning, implementation and monitoring of the GIM interventions in 16 states and UTs for which physical and financial targets were approved by the environment ministry during the period 2015-16 to 2024-25.Pointing out deficient monitoring, the CAG noted that 14 states even failed to provide required public web links for transparency. It flagged that audit evaluations revealed inflated data and overstated achievements, and GIS analysis showed that 70% of sampled sites had no noticeable changes attributable to GIM.

Article Title: ‘Since it’s written, it has to be done’: Law minister's delimitation push comes with Constitution jibe at Opp
Article Text:
Meghwal on delimitation and opposition

What is delimitation?

Join conversation View All Comments → Share your thoughts in the comments Insightful Agree Disagree Skeptical Concerning Promising Worth Reading Big Development Post Comment Be respectful · TOI community guidelines

Why were Lok Sabha seats frozen?

NEW DELHI: Union law minister Arjun Ram Meghwal on Thursday said delimitation is a “constitutional mandate” and asserted that the exercise must be carried out after 2026, as provided under the Constitution.Speaking in ANI , Meghwal criticised the Opposition over its objections to delimitation, saying that while opposition leaders “carry the Constitution around with them”, they do not read its provisions.“Delimitation is a constitutional mandate. They certainly carry the Constitution around with them, but they don't actually read what is written in it,” Meghwal said.He said the Constitution provides for the freezing of Lok Sabha seats until 2026, after which delimitation must take place.“Seats are to remain frozen until 2026, after which delimitation must take place. Since it is written there, it has to be done,” the Union minister said.The concerns are particularly among southern states, that a population-based redistribution could reduce their relative representation.Delimitation is the process of redrawing the boundaries of Lok Sabha and state assembly constituencies based on population.Under Article 82 of the Constitution, the exercise is to be carried out after every census.The aim is to ensure that constituencies have broadly similar population sizes, although their geographical areas can vary significantly. Each state is allocated a certain number of seats in Parliament and its assembly based on the population figures used for delimitation.India carried out delimitation exercises in 1952, 1962 and 1972. However, the 42nd Constitutional Amendment in 1976 froze the number of Lok Sabha seats based on the 1971 Census, in part to ensure that states that had successfully implemented population-control measures were not penalised with fewer parliamentary seats.The 84th Constitutional Amendment in 2001 extended the freeze on the allocation of seats among states until after 2026.A delimitation exercise was undertaken in 2008, but it used the 1971 Census to retain the existing distribution of Lok Sabha seats among states. It primarily involved redrawing constituency boundaries.
Article Summary: Delimitation is the process of redrawing the boundaries of Lok Sabha and state assembly constituencies based on population. The aim is to ensure that constituencies have broadly similar population sizes. Each state is allocated a certain number of seats in Parliament and its assembly based on the population figures used for delimitation.

Article Title: 'This is your last chance': SC ultimatum to Centre over delay in front-of-pack food warning labels
Article Text:

NEW DELHI: Supreme Court on Thursday sharply criticised the Centre and the Food Safety and Standards Authority of India FSSAI ) over the delay in introducing front-of-pack warning labels for packaged food products high in sugar, salt and saturated fat, warning that it would issue directions if the government failed to take a final decision.A bench of Justices JB Pardiwala and K Vinod Chandran gave the Centre two weeks to place its final decision on record, making it clear that the government could either implement the proposed warning labels on its own or face judicial intervention."This is your last chance. Next time we will dictate the judgment," the bench said, according to ANI.The court repeatedly underlined that the issue was one of public health, particularly the health of children and questioned the government's reluctance to move ahead with stronger nutritional warnings."Why? You don't want people of this country to remain healthy? More particularly growing children?" the bench asked during the hearing.Appearing for the Centre, additional solicitor general Brijender Chahar argued that applying strict warning standards could create complications for traditional Indian food items. He said products such as namkeen could end up carrying red warning symbols because of their fat or salt content.He also argued that international nutritional standards might not be directly applicable to Indian dietary habits, pointing out that even two eggs could exceed the prescribed daily fat limit.The court, however, was unconvinced.The bench said consumers were already aware that packaged foods contained sugar, fat and carbohydrates, but front-of-pack warning labels would provide a simpler and more effective way of communicating nutritional risks before a purchase was made.The judges also rejected the argument that warning labels could adversely affect manufacturers.According to ANI, the bench observed that the final decision to purchase a product would continue to rest with consumers and that commercial considerations could not take precedence over public health.During the proceedings, senior advocate Maninder Singh, appearing for a manufacturer, attempted to make submissions. The court responded by stating that the case concerned the health of citizens and that manufacturers could not determine government policy on the issue.Senior advocate Devadutt Kamat suggested that food products could be categorised differently and that detailed nutritional information should be displayed.The bench clarified that it was not opposed to any particular food product but was only seeking greater consumer awareness."In this country, how many people can afford dry fruits? And how many children buy Kurkure? That makes all the difference. We are not against any particular product. We only want the person purchasing it to know what he is consuming," the court said, according to ANI.The bench also referred to its February 10, 2026, order, in which it had previously addressed the issue and laid down its observations.During Thursday's hearing, the petitioner's counsel drew the court's attention to the minutes of an FSSAI meeting held on March 7, which allegedly reflected a position contrary to the suggestions made by the court earlier.The judges also took exception to the Centre's argument that India could not easily adopt international standards relating to nutritional warnings."We do not approve the stance of the Union when it says that it's not possible to match the international standards, more particularly developed countries. Should India remain an undeveloped country?" the bench asked, according to ANI."The world should know that India is concerned about the health of its citizens and more particularly children," it added.The case stems from a petition seeking mandatory front-of-pack warning labels for packaged food products containing high levels of sugar, salt and saturated fat.The proposed labels are intended to help consumers quickly identify potentially unhealthy products before buying them.The issue has also been discussed by Parliament's Committee on Subordinate Legislation, headed by Shiv Sena Rajya Sabha MP Milind Deora, who has advocated studying Singapore's Nutri-Grade model as a possible template for India.Separately, the Union health ministry has proposed displaying "sugar and oil boards" in schools, offices and other public institutions as part of a broader effort to encourage healthier eating habits and reduce excessive consumption of sugar and oil.
Article Summary: Justices JB Pardiwala and K Vinod Chandran gave the Centre two weeks to place its final decision on record. The court repeatedly underlined that the issue was one of public health, particularly the health of children. The proposed labels are intended to help consumers quickly identify potentially unhealthy products.

NEW DELHI: Parliament’s Monsoon Session ended on Thursday with both the Lok Sabha and Rajya Sabha being adjourned sine die, bringing to a close a session marked by repeated disruptions and protests by opposition parties.Parliamentary affairs minister Kiren Rijiju said the session was successful in terms of legislative business, with 12 Bills passed, but criticised the quality of debates and discussions.Addressing a press briefing, he said the government was not satisfied with the level of parliamentary discussion during the session.Rijiju said Lok Sabha productivity stood at 19% of the total allotted time, while Rajya Sabha recorded 39%.“The Monsoon Session concluded today. We view it from two perspectives. In terms of business, it was a very successful session; we passed a total of 12 bills. He said the Bills were discussed in the Rajya Sabha, although Congress and some other Opposition members staged a walkout.Rijiju said the Public Examinations (Prevention of Unfair Means) Bill was the only legislation to undergo a full discussion in the Lok Sabha during the session.“Only one bill, addressing the issue of paper leaks and unfair means in examinations, underwent a full discussion in the Lok Sabha,” he said.The legislation, which seeks to prevent unfair means in public examinations, was also discussed in the Rajya Sabha before being passed during the session.The Monsoon Session, which began on July 20, witnessed prolonged disruptions in both Houses.Opposition protests initially focused on the NEET paper leak and alleged irregularities involving donations to the Ram temple in Ayodhya.The opposition later sought discussions on police action against students protesting over the NEET issue and demanded statements from Prime Minister Narendra Modi and home minister Amit Shah.The government offered a discussion on the NEET paper leak and related issues, along with a reply from Shah, but the proposal was rejected by the Congress. Citing industry’s opposition to warning labels on food packets, the Food Safety and Standards Authority of India (FSSAI) has suggested a tabular declaration of the recommended daily requirement of added sugar, saturated fats and salt.The FSSAI’s affidavit filed in the Supreme Court only mentions the food industry’s opposition but has ignored the evidence in favour of warning label to help discourage consumption of foods high in added saturated fats, sugar and salt submitted by civil society representatives.FSSAI’s ‘compliance’ affidavit in response to the Supreme Court order directing it to frame Front of Pack labelling regulation states that a “majority of industry organizations were against the inclusion of ‘warning labels’ on the product,” and goes on to suggest a nutrition table giving “the daily allowance for added sugar, added saturated fat and salt vis a vis their presence in per serve of packed food product” on the front of the pack.“The proposed numerical table format being suggested by FSSAI would force consumers to do math at the supermarket shelf. The FSSAI has called it a ‘compliance’ affidavit but in reality, it is defiance. The Supreme Court had explicitly said that the exercise so far had not yielded any positive or good result and it had given FSSAI four weeks to revert. And six months later, FSSAI has filed an affidavit that abandons warning labels altogether and avoids defining HFSS (high fat, salt and sugar) foods.Clearly, FSSAI has bowed to food industry’s interests,” said Dr Arun Gupta of Nutrition Advocacy in Public Interest (NAPi).FSSAI stated in the affidavit that it had held a stakeholder consultation on March 19, 2026 involving consumer groups, food industry representatives and farmer organisations. It stated that industry bodies argued that “consumers should be able to make an informed decision without creating fear amongst the consumers”. The affidavit was silent on the input given by consumer organisations, which had sought warning labels that have been shown to be the most effective in reducing consumption of junk food high in salt, sugar and saturated fats in several countries. NAPi had also given FSSAI evidence generated from studies conducted in India and other countries showing how effective warning labels are.

NEW DELHI: The Centre has formally notified the BHAVYA Rasayan scheme to establish three greenfield chemical parks across the country, paving the way for states to compete for projects aimed at boosting domestic chemical manufacturing, reducing import dependence and attracting investment.The Gazette notification issued by the Ministry of Chemicals and Fertilisers operationalises the scheme approved by the Union Cabinet last month. With a total outlay of Rs 3,030 crore, the scheme will run from 2026-27 to 2030-31 and support the creation of shared industrial infrastructure for the chemical sector.Under the scheme, the Centre will provide up to Rs 1,000 crore for each chemical park, subject to the concerned state contributing at least Rs 500 crore. Any expenditure beyond this will have to be borne by the state government. Each park must have a minimum 8 sq km (2,000 acres) of contiguous, encumbrance-free land.The parks will be selected through a challenge-based competitive process, with proposals evaluated on predefined quantitative and qualitative parameters, including strategic relevance, financial viability, implementation plans and long-term sustainability.According to the notification, the parks will provide common facilities such as central effluent treatment plants, hazardous waste management systems, water supply, solvent recovery and distillation units, steam generation and distribution networks, interconnected pipelines, logistics infrastructure, laboratory testing centres and emergency response facilities, enabling industries to reduce costs and improve environmental compliance.The government said the scheme is aimed at strengthening the entire chemical value chain, enhancing domestic production capacity, improving cost competitiveness, promoting exports and import substitution, attracting domestic and foreign investment, and generating employment, while contributing to the goal of Viksit Bharat 2047.
Article Summary: The scheme will run from 2026-27 to 2030-31 and support the creation of shared industrial infrastructure for the chemical sector. Article Title: From New York to Delaware: US states to commemorate 'India Day' on August 15
Article Text:
US states proclaim August 15 as 'India Day' (representative image)

Delaware honours Indian-American community

New York, New Jersey also recognise August 15

How US communities celebrate India's Independence Day

India marks 80th Independence Day with focus on youth

Delaware has proclaimed August 15, 2026, as ‘India Day’, joining New York and New Jersey in recognising India's Independence Day and the contributions of the Indian-American community ahead of the country's 80th Independence Day.The proclamation was issued by Delaware Governor Matthew Meyer, who highlighted the state's growing Indian-American community and its contributions to the state's social and economic life.The development was shared by the Consulate General of India in New York on August 13.According to the proclamation, Delaware is strengthened by the many cultures and traditions represented across its communities, including its Indian-American population.The proclamation said Delawareans of Indian heritage have enriched the state through their work, leadership and service, contributing to shared prosperity and creating opportunities for future generations.It also highlighted India's diversity of languages, traditions, faiths and customs, noting that generations of Indian Americans have carried these traditions forward while building communities in the US.The proclamation said India Day would provide an opportunity to honour India's independence, celebrate the heritage and achievements of Delaware's Indian-American community and recognise the enduring connections between Delaware and the people of India.Governor Meyer encouraged residents to participate in the observance and recognise the contributions of the state's Indian-American community.Delaware's proclamation follows similar declarations by New York and New Jersey, which recognised August 15, as India's Independence Day.New Jersey governor Mikie Sherrill issued a proclamation recognising Indian Independence Day across the state. According to the Consulate General of India in New York, the proclamation highlighted the Indian-American community's contributions to New Jersey in areas including education, healthcare, research, technology, business, public service and community leadership.New York Governor Kathy Hochul also proclaimed August 15 as India Independence Day across the state.The Consulate said New York's proclamation recognised the Indian-American community's contribution to the state's cultural, economic and civic life, while also highlighting the enduring ties between India and the US.The Consulate thanked Hochul for the recognition, saying the proclamation celebrated India's journey of independence and the democratic values shared by the two countries.India's Independence Day is marked across the US each year through flag-hoisting ceremonies, parades, cultural programmes and community events.Indian diplomatic missions, including the Embassy of India in Washington and Indian consulates, hold special programmes on August 15. The Indian mission to the United Nations also participates in commemorative events.Indian-American communities across states organise cultural performances and public celebrations, with local political leaders often participating and highlighting the community's contributions to American society.Prominent landmarks have also joined the celebrations in previous years, including the Empire State Building in New York and the Space Needle in Seattle, which have been illuminated in the colours of the Indian tricolour for Independence Day events.The proclamations come as India prepares to celebrate its 80th Independence Day on August 15, 2026.This year's celebrations will also focus on the commemoration of 150 years of ‘Vande Mataram’, while placing particular emphasis on ‘Yuva Shakti’ or youth power.The celebrations are expected to combine the historical significance of India's freedom movement with recognition of the achievements and contributions of its younger generation.The growing number of US states formally recognising India's Independence Day also underlines the visibility of the Indian-American community and the broader social, economic and cultural ties between India and the United States.
Article Summary: Delaware joins New York and New Jersey in recognising India's Independence Day. Proclamation was issued by Governor Matthew Meyer, who highlighted the state's growing Indian-American community. New York Governor Kathy Hochul also proclaimed August 15 as India Independence Day across the state. The proclamations come as India prepares to celebrate its 80th Independence Day on August 15, 2026.

The decision to refer the bill to JPC was made by a voice vote.

NEW DELHI: The Joint Action Forum on Minorities that had led a delegation of representatives of Churches to meet Home Minister Amit Shah last week described the decision of the govt to refer the FCRA Amendment Bill 2026 to a Joint Parliamentary Committee as a “positive step” that presents an “important opportunity for a comprehensive, clause-by-clause review of its provisions and their implications”.A host of Church bodies last week met and urged home minister Amit Shah to either withdraw the Foreign Contribution (Regulation) Amendment Bill or send it to a joint parliamentary committee for scrutiny.In their representation to HM, the delegation representing Catholic, Protestant and Orthodox Churches from across India organised under Joint Action Forum on Minorities with DMK MP P Wilson as its chairperson, had sought that the Bill is withdrawn in entirety or in alternate be referred to a Joint Parliamentary Committee together with a review of the working of the Principal FCRA Act 2010 itself".On Wednesday, Wilson in a statement on X thanked DMK President MK Stalin and all opposition parties in the Lok Sabha for their unified demand to withdraw the FCRA Amendment Bill 2026, even though it was decided by a majority voice vote to refer it to the Joint Parliamentary Committee.“Although the govt has not agreed to withdraw the FCRA Bill 2026 entirely, the Union Government's decision to refer the Bill to the Joint Parliamentary Committee is a positive step,” he added.“This is a sensitive issue where a balance must be struck between the govt’s authority over financial control and the rights of minority institutions to receive charitable contributions. This funding supports schools, colleges, hospitals, and other public service institutions. The government will be unable to fund these activities if contributions cease,” he added.Wilson said that the referral of the Bill to the JPC presents an important opportunity for a comprehensive, clause-by-clause review of its provisions and their implications. “We hope and expect that the Committee will listen to all stakeholders and carefully consider the constitutional, legal, and practical concerns raised by religious, educational, healthcare, charitable, and civil society institutions,” he said.The National Council of Churches in India, General Secretary, Asir Ebenezer welcomed the Bill and said that they look forward to engaging with “the JPC as they prepare the report for the Winter session”. Article Title: ‘Sushmita Dev called me lungi wala’: CPM’s John Brittas on BJP MP; uproar in Rajya Sabha over alleged remark

Article Title: Congress spent Rs 248.6 crore on 5-state polls, received Rs 207.1 crore during election period

As part of general party propaganda, the Congress spent Rs 92.5 crore on media advertisements (representative image)

NEW DELHI: The Congress spent a total Rs 248.6 crore on its campaign for the recent assembly elections in Assam, Kerala, Tamil Nadu, West Bengal and Puducherry, even as its total receipts between the date of announcement and completion of these polls stood at Rs 207.1 crore.According to Congress's election expenditure statement for the five state/UT polls, filed on July 31 with the Election Commission, the party received Rs 104 crore in cash and Rs 103.1 crore via cheque or draft between March 15, 2026, when the elections were announced, and May 6, 2026, when they had concluded.The Congress's full poll expense statement shows its total opening balance of cash in hand (including at the level of its central headquarters and the state/district/local level units of the 5 states/UTs) at Rs 22.9 crore and its cash in bank at Rs 146.1 crore. At the end of the polls, its cash in hand was marginally lower at Rs 22.6 crore while its bank balance had declined by 45% to Rs 80.6 crore.On the expenditure side, the party declared a total spend of Rs 143 crore on general party propaganda and Rs 105.6 crore on candidates. The latter includes Rs 95.5 crore given by the party as lump-sum payments to its candidates across the five poll-gone states/UT; while the central party headquarters bore Rs 95.3 crore of expenditure under this head, the state/district/local units disbursed only Rs 23 lakh among the candidates.Expenses on virtual campaigns through social media platforms and applications were declared at Rs 6.8 crore.Over Rs 3.2 crore was spent by the Congress on publicising the criminal antecedents of its candidates.As part of general party propaganda, the Congress spent Rs 92.5 crore on media advertisements, covering print and electronic space, bulk SMS, cable TV, websites and TV channels. Another Rs 8 crore funded public meetings, processions and rallies, while Rs 11.5 crore was spent on badges, posters, cutouts, hoardings etc and nearly Rs 2 crore on miscellaneous propaganda items.Poll surveys and campaigns for the five assembly elections cost the Congress Rs 4.8 crore.A total Rs 23.5 crore was spent by the grand old party on the travel and lodging of its star campaigners (Rs 21.8 crore) and other leaders. The aircraft and helicopters were sourced from Air Charter Services Pvt Ltd, Aircab Aviation, A R Airways, GMP Air Charter, Lima Tang Aviation Service, Devigo Data Systems and Global Vectra.The Congress's central headquarters routed Rs 83.2 crore of its lump-sum payments to candidates through the state/UT units; with Kerala unit getting the largest share at Rs 55.1 crore, followed by Puducherry (Rs 10 crore), West Bengal (Rs 9 crore), Tamil Nadu (Rs 7.1 crore) and Assam (Rs 2 crore).The Congress-led UDF seized power in Kerala, but the party or its alliances performed poorly in other states, managing 21 seats in Assam, 6 in Puducherry and 2 in West Bengal, while drawing a blank in Tamil Nadu.
Article Summary: The Congress spent a total Rs 248.6 crore on its campaign for the recent assembly elections. The party received Rs 104 crore in cash and Rs 103.1 crore via cheque or draft. As part of general party propaganda, the Congress spent Rs 92.5 crore on media advertisements.

Article Title: ‘MPs should not be reduced’: Udhayanidhi Stalin backs TVK's resolution against delimitation
Article Text:
DMK backs Tamil Nadu’s delimitation resolution
