NEW DELHI: DMK on Wednesday supported the Tamil Nadu government’s resolution opposing the Centre’s proposed delimitation exercise, with Leader of Opposition Udhayanidhi Stalin saying the state’s representation in the Lok Sabha should not be reduced.He said the number of Members of Parliament from Tamil Nadu should not be reduced in the name of delimitation and called for the exercise to be deferred for 25 years."In the name of constituency delimitation, the number of Members of Parliament should not be reduced. Our stand is that constituency delimitation should not be carried out for the next 25 years. We welcome the resolution on the 33% reservation for women. Our firm stand is that Tamil Nadu should not be affected by constituency delimitation. The movement that first told India what the impact of delimitation would be is the DMK," Udhayanidhi added.The development comes after Tamil Nadu assembly on Wednesday passed a resolution in the state Assembly opposing the Union government’s proposed delimitation exercise.Speaking in the assembly, CM Vijay also called for the implementation of 33 per cent reservation for women in the 2029 Lok Sabha elections based on the existing 543 constituencies."The 33% reservation for women should be implemented in the 2029 Lok Sabha elections itself, based on the existing 543 constituencies. The 33% reservation for women should not be delayed any further. In Tamil Nadu, more women have voted than men. Providing reservation for women is not a concession; it is a matter of social justice. The 33% reservation for women must be implemented without any further delay," he said.The resolution seeks to safeguard the political representation of southern states, particularly Tamil Nadu, arguing that their success in controlling population growth should not result in reduced representation in Parliament."All the states including Tamil Nadu and the people / elected representatives of the union territories have not had their population counted for more than 50 years. The next census to count the population was supposed to be held in 2026. Therefore, since the delimitation of constituencies has not been carried out for the last 50 years, based on the 2011 population census, the constituencies should be delimited and the number of Lok Sabha and Assembly members should be increased from 550 to 850 by bringing in a constitutional amendment Bill," the resolution stated.The Constitution (131st Amendment) Bill, 2026, was introduced in the Lok Sabha on April 16, proposing to increase the strength of the Lower House to 850 seats and expedite the implementation of the Women's Reservation Bill passed in 2023. However, the Bill failed to secure the constitutionally required two-thirds majority of members present and voting and was not passed.While the Congress and other opposition parties have supported the Women's Reservation Bill, they have opposed the proposed delimitation exercise and called for an increase in the number of Lok Sabha seats. The Opposition has also demanded that women's reservation be delinked from delimitation.
Article Summary: DMK supports Tamil Nadu government's resolution opposing Centre's proposed delimitation exercise. Leader of Opposition Udhayanidhi Stalin says state's representation in Lok Sabha should not be reduced. Tamil Nadu assembly on Wednesday passed a resolution in the state Assembly opposing the Union government's proposed exercise.

Article Title: 5 indigenous small modular reactors targeted by 2033, Jitendra Singh tells LS
Article Text:
Union MoS Jitendra Singh speaks in the Lok Sabha during the Monsoon session of Parliament

Join conversation View All Comments → Share your thoughts in the comments Insightful Agree Disagree Skeptical Concerning Promising Worth Reading Big Development Post Comment Be respectful · TOI community guidelines

NEW DELHI: A key objective of the govt under the Nuclear Energy Mission is to develop and operationalise at least five indigenous small modular reactors by 2033, minister for department of atomic energy Jitendra Singh said in a written reply in the Lok Sabha on Wednesday.Bhabha Atomic Research Centre (BARC) is undertaking the design and development of indigenous SMR technologies, including the 220 MWe Bharat Small Modular Reactor (BSMR-200) and 55 MWe SMR-55 for power generation. BARC is also developing a high temperature gas cooled reactor (HTGCR) of up to 5 MW capacity, which can be coupled with a suitable thermochemical cycle for hydrogen production.Singh said India is steadily strengthening its indigenous nuclear energy ecosystem with a focus on advanced reactor technologies, SMRs, domestic manufacturing capabilities, private-sector participation and long-term utilisation of the country’s abundant thorium resources. The govt has adopted a two-pronged approach to accelerate nuclear capacity addition. This includes deployment of large indigenous reactors such as 700 MWe pressurised heavy water reactors (PHWRs) and advanced reactor designs at greenfield sites, alongside development and deployment of SMRs at brownfield locations, including retiring fossil-fuel-based power plants, captive plants for energy-intensive industries and off-grid applications in remote areas.The minister also highlighted continuing work of the Indira Gandhi Centre for Atomic Research (IGCAR) in advancing the second stage of India’s nuclear power programme. IGCAR is pursuing multidisciplinary scientific research and advanced engineering development for sodium cooled fast breeder reactors and associated closed fuel-cycle facilities, technologies that remain a cornerstone of India’s long-term nuclear strategy.On thorium, Singh said India is pursuing its three-stage nuclear power programme, based on a closed fuel cycle, to optimise utilisation of its uranium resources and progressively harness its abundant thorium reserves. Thorium, being a fertile material, needs to be converted into fissile uranium-233 in a nuclear reactor before it can be used for energy generation.India has already undertaken sustained R&D towards thorium utilisation. Thorium Oxide (Thoria) pellets have been used in the initial cores of operating PHWRs, while Thoria-based fuels have also been irradiated in BARC research reactors. The irradiated Thoria pins have been reprocessed to obtain uranium-233, which has subsequently been fabricated as fuel for the KAMINI reactor at IGCAR, Kalpakkam. Singh said the Sustainable Harnessing and Advancement of Nuclear Energy for Transforming India (SHANTI) Act, 2025 has been enacted to enable wider participation of both public and private entities in the nuclear sector.
Article Summary: The govt under the Nuclear Energy Mission is to develop and operationalise at least five indigenous small modular reactors by 2033. Bhabha Atomic Research Centre (BARC) is undertaking the design and development of indigenous SMR technologies. The govt has adopted a two-pronged approach to accelerate nuclear capacity addition.

Article Title: Supreme Court pushes 19 states, union territories to notify cancer
Article Text:
Supreme Court has stepped up efforts to bring greater uniformity to cancer reporting

Join conversation View All Comments → Share your thoughts in the comments Insightful Agree Disagree Skeptical Concerning Promising Worth Reading Big Development Post Comment Be respectful · TOI community guidelines

NEW DELHI: With the National Cancer Registry Programme covering only a fraction of India’s population and rural cancer surveillance remaining particularly limited, the Supreme Court has stepped up efforts to bring greater uniformity to cancer reporting. The court on Tuesday asked the 19 States and Union Territories that have not yet notified cancer as a notifiable disease to consider doing so, a move that could make reporting of newly detected cases to public health authorities mandatory.Such notification could help plug gaps in cancer surveillance by giving health authorities a more complete picture of the country’s cancer burden, including where cases are rising and which populations are most affected. The data could in turn help shape policies on prevention, early detection, treatment capacity and allocation of healthcare resources.A bench headed by Chief Justice Surya Kant passed the order on a plea filed by a retired AIIMS doctor after his lawyer Gaurav Bansal told the court that NCRP covers only 10% of population and rural coverage is less than 1%.The push assumes greater significance against the backdrop of the WHO’s latest Global Status Report on Cancer, which estimates that 92% of people globally will be affected by cancer either directly or through a close family member.The report also projects annual cancer cases to rise to nearly 35 million by 2050.The Supreme Court was informed that 17 of India’s 36 States and UTs have already notified cancer, following recommendations of the Parliamentary Standing Committee on Health and Family Welfare. The remaining 19 have now been asked to consider similar action.Dr Pragya Shukla, Head of Clinical Oncology at Delhi State Cancer Institute, said standardised, disease-specific and timely data was essential to track India's changing cancer burden, identify regional and demographic trends, and assess the impact of prevention and treatment programmes. Such a system, she said, would complement existing cancer registries, help identify high-burden areas, improve planning for treatment infrastructure and medicines, and strengthen evidence-based cancer control. Govil added that reliable data would be critical for planning prevention, early detection and resource allocation.The Indian Cancer Society welcomed the intervention, saying national notification could help build a comprehensive cancer surveillance system. “The Supreme Court’s intervention is a significant development, and we welcome its direction to the remaining States and Union Territories to move towards cancer notification,” said Jyotsna Govil, Chairperson, Indian Cancer Society, Delhi. However, she stressed that notification alone would not suffice and called for a uniform national framework with common definitions, reporting standards and data protocols to ensure comparable and interoperable data across states.
Article Summary: Supreme Court has stepped up efforts to bring greater uniformity to cancer reporting. The court on Tuesday asked the 19 States and Union Territories that have not yet notified cancer as a notifiable disease to consider doing so. The move could make reporting of newly detected cases to public health authorities mandatory.

Article Title: Explosion at Europe's largest port kills one, injures six as investigators probe cause
Article Text:
Blast at Rotterdam petroleum storage facility kills one, injures six during maintenance work

A blast at a petroleum storage facility in the Netherlands' Rotterdam port killed one person and injured six others on Thursday, with authorities investigating the cause of the explosion.The blast occurred at around 11.30 am local time during maintenance work on a storage tank operated by energy commodities trader Gunvor. A company spokesperson described it as an “incident” and said Gunvor was cooperating with authorities.Police said there was no immediate indication of sabotage, but all possible causes were being considered.The explosion took place at the Port of Rotterdam, Europe's largest port and a major centre for oil and fuel imports and storage. The sprawling facility also houses major refineries operated by Shell, BP, ExxonMobil and Vitol.Shell said its operations were unaffected, while the port said its LNG terminals were not hit by the blast. Gas flows at Rotterdam's Gate LNG terminal briefly dipped before becoming volatile, although it was unclear whether that was linked to the explosion or a separate power outage elsewhere in the port.ExxonMobil said a power outage affecting its 191,000-barrel-per-day refinery had been resolved and that operations were normal.Rotterdam Port and local authorities said the outage was unrelated to the blast.The incident is being closely watched because the port is a major energy hub for northwestern Europe. The Gate terminal is one of the region's key LNG import facilities, while Dutch gas storage levels are currently around 40% ahead of the winter heating season.
Article Summary: Blast occurred during maintenance work on a storage tank operated by energy commodities trader Gunvor. Police said there was no immediate indication of sabotage, but all possible causes were being considered. Gas flows at Rotterdam's Gate LNG terminal briefly dipped before becoming volatile.

Article Title: Who is Gautam Rangarajan? Indian-origin strategist appointed to key role by UK PM Andy Burnham
Article Text:
Indian-origin strategist Gautam Rangarajan.

Who is Gautam Rangarajan ?

What will Gautam Rangarajan do at No. 10?

Burnham's government overhaul

British Prime Minister Andy Burnham has appointed Indian-origin strategist and former BBC executive Gautam Rangarajan as an Expert Adviser on Structure and Process in a newly created role at 10 Downing Street.Rangarajan, who brings decades of experience in strategy, organisational transformation and media, is set to take up the position this week.Rangarajan is a senior strategist and media executive with more than two decades of experience across media, creative industries and public service broadcasting.Before his new government role, he spent more than 30 years at the BBC, beginning his career as a radio music producer and eventually rising to become the broadcaster's Group Director for Strategy and Performance.His experience includes developing strategy in rapidly changing markets, leading large-scale transformation initiatives and handling complex policy and financial negotiations.The exact details of Rangarajan's responsibilities are yet to be outlined. However, the UK PM's office said his appointment draws on his experience in corporate strategy and transformation.His role comes as Burnham undertakes a broader restructuring of the machinery of government, including the creation of the Office for the Prime Minister and Cabinet.Rangarajan is expected to play a role in the planned transformation at the heart of the British government.Away from strategy and public service, Rangarajan also has a creative side. He describes himself as a professional choral singer and music producer, alongside his work in corporate strategy and organisational transformation.The appointment comes as Burnham reshapes his government following his recent rise to the role of Labour Party leader and Prime Minister.His administration has announced structural changes, including the launch of No. 10 North in Manchester and the creation of the Office for the Prime Minister and Cabinet.While the full scope of Rangarajan's new role remains unclear, his appointment places the former BBC executive at the centre of the UK government's planned transformation.
Article Summary: Gautam Rangarajan is a senior strategist and media executive. He has more than two decades of experience across media, creative industries and public service broadcasting. His appointment places the former BBC executive at the centre of the UK government's planned transformation.

Article Title: In 2020, Minnesota funded a $1.918 million Shell Rock River habitat program; by 2025, it had protected or restored 588 acres
Article Text:
Shell Rock River Watershed District (Image Credit: www.shellrock.org)

A habitat program takes shape

Three properties protected

Wetlands and prairie restored

More acres than planned

A longer-term conservation effort

In 2020, Minnesota approved $1.918 million for the Shell Rock River Watershed Habitat Restoration Program - Phase IX. According to a 2025 final report from the Lessard-Sams Outdoor Heritage Council, the program ultimately protected, restored or enhanced 588 acres of habitat in the Shell Rock River watershed, exceeding its original goal of 483 acres.The funding was provided under Minnesota Laws 2020, with the appropriation directed to the Minnesota Department of Natural Resources for an agreement with the Shell Rock River Watershed District. The funding was intended to support land acquisition as well as the restoration and enhancement of aquatic habitat within the watershed. The program focused on several types of conservation work, including acquiring properties, restoring wetlands and improving aquatic habitat. The projects were selected using conservation planning and monitoring intended to identify areas where habitat improvements could provide significant benefits.The Shell Rock River Watershed is a shallow-lake system that supports fish, waterfowl and other wildlife. According to the final report, restoration projects were targeted at addressing habitat degradation and improving conditions for native fish, waterfowl and wildlife.One part of Phase IX involved acquiring three properties: the Glenville Property, the Bancroft Property, and the Church Lake Property. The District closed on the Glenville Property in March 2021 and the Bancroft Property in September 2021. For the Church Lake Property, the District transferred the deed to the Minnesota Department of Natural Resources in December 2024 after acquiring and restoring the parcel.The final report says these acquisitions contributed to the program's permanent protection of 218 acres. Another 370 acres of habitat and wetlands were enhanced or restored through the program. Together, those accomplishments contributed to the reported total of 588 acres protected, enhanced or restored.The program included several restoration projects beyond property acquisition. The Bancroft Wetland Restoration was initiated in 2020, with construction beginning in June 2024 and largely completed by the fall of that year. Additional seeding work was completed in spring 2025. Another project focused on Panicum Prairie, where habitat enhancement work was carried out across 300 acres. The project involved native prairie vegetation and was substantially completed in February 2025, with final work completed in May.The program also supported the Fountain Lake In-Lake Habitat Project. Work included additional rock reefs and rock boulder clusters intended to improve fish habitat. The report notes that Phase IX funds were used to expand the scope of this work after the District determined additional funds were available. These projects addressed different parts of the watershed's ecosystem, from wetlands and prairie habitat to aquatic areas. The broader aim was to improve habitat conditions while protecting areas that could provide long-term benefits for wildlife.The program's original accomplishment plan called for 483 acres. By the end of the project, the final total had reached 588 acres, 105 acres more than initially planned. The report attributes the increase to the addition of the In-Lake Habitat Project and the Church Lake Property to Phase IX.According to the report, all grant funds were spent. The final grant expenditure remained $1.918 million, while the program's final total including leverage was $1.9479 million.The work is intended to continue beyond the end of the grant. The Shell Rock River Watershed District relies on multiple funding sources, including a local option sales tax, local levy and public funding, to maintain conservation projects. The Minnesota Department of Natural Resources will also maintain the Church Lake Property, which it owns.The program's results illustrate how a single state-funded conservation effort can combine land protection, wetland restoration, prairie enhancement and aquatic habitat improvements. Rather than focusing on one habitat type, Phase IX combined several projects across the Shell Rock River watershed. By 2025, the program had moved beyond its original target, with the final report recording 588 acres protected, enhanced or restored. The completed work represents a combination of permanent land protection and habitat improvements designed to support Minnesota's fish, waterfowl and wildlife over the long term.
Article Summary: In 2020, Minnesota approved $1.918 million for the Shell Rock River Watershed Habitat Restoration Program - Phase IX. By 2025, the program had moved beyond its original target, with the final report recording 588 acres protected, enhanced or restored.

Article Title: Gates Foundation donates $540 million grant to University of Washington for research on…
Article Text:
Gates Foundation makes one of its biggest investments in health research

Gates Foundation's $540 million grant to expand health research

Long partnership between Gates Foundation and IHME

The Gates Foundation has announced a $540 million grant to the Institute for Health Metrics and Evaluation (IHME) at the University of Washington, marking one of its biggest investments in health research. As reported by Fortune, the 10-year funding will help expand global health data and research used by governments and policymakers to respond to disease outbreaks and improve healthcare. The donations come as the US government continues to reduce funding for scientific research, public health, education and other programmes, the report says, adding that the billionaire philanthropy is increasingly filling gaps left by federal funding cuts in the US.Gates Foundation's $540 million grant will allow IHME to expand its Global Burden of Disease study, which measures diseases, injuries and health risks across the world. According to the foundation, the project will increase its coverage from about 925 locations to nearly 5,000, giving governments and researchers more detailed local health data to support policy decisions.“Reliable and independent evidence can mean the difference between reacting to a health crisis after it has taken hold and acting early enough to change its course,” said Dr.Christopher J.L. Murray, IHME director and professor of health metrics sciences.“This investment will allow us to provide high-quality evidence at a much more local level and help leaders understand not only where health is improving or worsening, but which decisions can make the greatest difference for people,” he added.The latest funding builds on a long relationship between the Gates Foundation and IHME. The foundation provided the original funding to establish the research institute at the University of Washington in 2007. Since then, IHME has become one of the world's leading sources of public health data and disease research.Gates Foundation to shut down operations by 2045Gates Foundation has previously announced plans to wind down operations by 2045 and significantly increase its charitable spending over the next two decades. Earlier this year, the foundation said it would distribute $9 billion in 2026 while reducing its workforce as part of preparations for its planned closure. Bill Gates has also pledged to give away almost all of his wealth, with the foundation planning to spend more than $200 billion by 2045.
Article Summary: The Gates Foundation has announced a $540 million grant to the Institute for Health Metrics and Evaluation (IHME) at the University of Washington. The 10-year funding will help expand global health data and research used by governments and policymakers. The donations come as the US government continues to reduce funding for scientific research, public health, education and other programmes.

Article Title: Nick Long, Mayor of League City in Texas, joins H-1B visa debate; says: H-1B program should not be used by any ...

Public universities are H-1B cap-exempt

The filing prompted Scott Bowen, Republican nominee for Texas House of Representatives, to share the post on his timeline writing: “Texas State graduates hundreds of communication majors every year. Not one of them was qualified for this job?”.Nick Long quoted the post and wrote: “No public entity should be using H-1B program. Taxpayers should get taxpayer funded jobs”.Under the Immigration and Nationality Act (INA § 214(g)(5)(A) and (B)), certain categories of H1B petitions are exempt from the annual numerical cap of 65,000 (plus 20,000 master's cap). This means they can sponsor eligible foreign workers for H-1B visas throughout the year without participating in the annual lottery.The exemption also applies to nonprofit entities affiliated with higher education institutions and certain nonprofit or government research organisations.In other news, a new research indicates a projected decline in international student enrollment for Fall 2026. Preliminary analysis by NAFSA: Association of International Educators and JB International shows cascading effects on US economic contribution and jobs supported. This downturn reflects the convergence of several headwinds: declining application volumes, persistent visa appointment bottlenecks, and newly restrictive immigration policy changes.
Article Summary: The debate began after Texas State University filed a notice of intent to sponsor an H-1B visa for a Public Relations Specialist position. Nick Long quoted the post and wrote: “No public entity should be using H- 1B program. Taxpayers should get taxpayer funded jobs’

Article Title: TCS, Vodafone partner on AI-led digital transformation
Article Text: Tata Consultancy Services (TCS), a global leader in IT services, consulting, and business solutions, has announced a strategic partnership with Vodafone Business, the enterprise arm of VodafoneThree, the UK’s largest mobile operator. The partnership aims to help customers modernise technology, accelerate digital adoption, reduce complexity, and scale to achieve stronger business outcomes and enhanced customer experience.The collaboration will span priority areas including cloud transformation and migration, AI and automation, cyber security, network modernisation, digital infrastructure, data and analytics, IoT and connected business applications, managed services, and operational transformation.Through this agreement, TCS will help Vodafone Business strengthen its ability to support UK organisations with secure, resilient, and scalable digital foundations for growth. The partnership builds on VodafoneThree’s £11 billion investment to create the UK’s best network for business, empowering customers across public sector, healthcare, financial services, manufacturing, retail, and critical national infrastructure sectors.Nick Gliddon, Business Director, VodafoneThree, said: “UK businesses are looking for partners who understand their market, their customers, and the pressure to modernise quickly. The challenge for many organisations is not ambition, it is execution… We are pleased to welcome TCS to our growing ecosystem of strategic partners.”Vinay Singvi, Head of UK and Ireland, TCS, added: “We see enormous potential to leverage AI and digital transformation, scale of operating model, deep technology expertise, and wide industry domain experiences to unlock greater value for Vodafone Business, TCS, and its customers in the UK.”The partnership builds on TCS’s long-standing commitment to the UK, where it has invested in innovation, talent, and enterprise transformation for over 50 years. TCS has created 42,000 jobs in the country and continues to foster collaboration through initiatives such as its AI Experience Zone and London Design Studio, part of its flagship TCS PacePort facility.
Article Summary: Tata Consultancy Services (TCS) has announced a strategic partnership with Vodafone Business. The partnership aims to help customers modernise technology, accelerate digital adoption, reduce complexity, and scale. The collaboration will span priority areas including cloud transformation and migration.

Article Title: Iran war risk: JPMorgan CEO Jamie Dimon warns of oil shocks, sticky inflation and higher interest rates
Article Text: JPMorgan Chase CEO Jamie Dimon has warned that the ongoing war in Iran could trigger oil and commodity price shocks, keeping inflation elevated and pushing interest rates higher than current market expectations, Reuters reported.The warning came in his annual letter to shareholders, a day after US President Donald Trump escalated pressure on Iran by threatening to target key infrastructure if the Strait of Hormuz is not reopened."Now, because of the war in Iran, we additionally face the potential for significant ongoing oil and commodity price shocks, along with the reshaping of global supply chains, which may lead to stickier inflation and ultimately higher interest rates than markets currently expect," Dimon said, news agency Reuters quoted as saying.Dimon, who has led JPMorgan for two decades, also highlighted broader geopolitical risks, including the war in Ukraine, tensions in the Middle East and friction with China."The challenges we all face are significant," he added.He said it remains uncertain whether the Iran war will achieve US objectives, while warning that nuclear proliferation remains the biggest risk linked to Iran.Markets have already begun pricing in these risks, with expectations of interest rate cuts this year largely fading amid rising inflation concerns triggered by the conflict.Last week, the benchmark S&P 500 index recorded its worst quarterly performance since 2022, weighed down by rising energy prices and geopolitical uncertainty since late February.Dimon noted that the US economy remains resilient, with consumers continuing to earn and spend, and businesses staying broadly healthy, though signs of weakening have emerged.He cautioned that economic strength has been supported by significant government deficit spending and past stimulus, while infrastructure investment needs continue to grow.At the same time, he pointed to positives such as fiscal stimulus under President Trump's "Big, Beautiful Bill", deregulation policies and rising capital expenditure driven by artificial intelligence.On financial stability, Dimon said the $1.8-trillion private credit market "probably" does not pose a systemic risk, despite investor concerns and recent withdrawals from such funds.However, he warned that in a downturn, losses across leveraged lending could exceed expectations as credit standards have weakened.Private credit markets also lack transparency and rigorous valuation benchmarks, increasing the risk of investor exits if conditions worsen, he said.Separately, Dimon criticised revised US capital rules, including Basel III and GSIB surcharge norms, calling aspects of the proposals "nonsensical" and "very flawed".He said JPMorgan’s GSIB surcharge would fall only to 5.0%, a level he described as “absurd” and “un-American”, arguing it penalises the bank’s scale and performance.
Article Summary: JPMorgan Chase CEO Jamie Dimon warns Iran war could trigger oil and commodity price shocks. He also highlighted broader geopolitical risks, including the war in Ukraine, tensions in the Middle East and friction with China. Dimon criticised revised US capital rules, including Basel III and GSIB surcharge norms, calling aspects of the proposals "nonsensical"

Article Title: How selling Alaska in 1867 was a costly mistake for Russia
Article Text:
Image: Wikipedia

Why Russia agreed to the Alaska purchase

The hidden wealth Russia gave away

Strategic and geopolitical consequences







In 1867, Russia’s decision to sell Alaska to America turned out to be a historic mistake that was to go unnoticed for years to come. The sum paid by the US was only $7,200,000. Although, in the light of the circumstances at the time, it appeared logical, retrospectively, the act looks extremely shortsighted. Russia found itself economically constrained, geographically far away from the region and fearful of its falling into the hands of the British without any compensation. In reality, however, the region had proved immensely valuable both strategically and naturally. Its vast reserves of oil, gold, and natural resources would later transform it into one of the most economically significant territories in the United States.The choice of selling Alaska was based on economic and political reasons. By the middle of the 19th century, the Russian Empire experienced financial difficulties as a result of the expensive Crimean War. It had become increasingly hard for the country to manage such remote and thinly populated areas as Alaska.According to EBSCO , “the Russian-American Company was in decline, and the colony failed to yield any profit”.In addition to this, the lucrative fur trade had declined, making the territory much less economically valuable for the empire.At the same time, Russia was afraid that Britain might capture Alaska in case another war broke out between the two countries. Selling the colony to the friendly United States appeared as a logical step. As the Office of the Historian states, William H. Seward, U.S. Secretary of State, “it was a chance to expand its influence in North America and hinder further growth of Britain”.For Russia, the transaction was a chance to minimise the losses. However, it greatly undervalued the potential of Alaska.Another thing that Russia did not expect was the amount of riches that Alaska possessed. Within several decades after the acquisition, the state saw discoveries of enormous deposits of gold, oil, and other minerals.“Alaska has produced more than 40 million ounces of gold,” according to the US Geological Survey. Furthermore, Alaska is home to some of the world's most significant undeveloped mineral deposits, according to the U.S. Geological Survey (USGS) . But even more importantly, the state's oil deposits turned out to be extremely valuable. The Prudhoe Bay oil field was discovered in 1968 and became one of North America's biggest.In retrospect, the amount paid by the Americans, $7.2 million, or two cents per acre, was rather laughable. According to Howard I. Kushner , the deal “robbed Russia of an enormously rich territory, the true value of which would only be recognised in the twentieth century.”In addition to resources, there is the question of strategy and how important Alaska is to the United States from a strategic standpoint. This is a very good place when it comes to defence strategy. It borders on the Arctic Ocean and also happens to be close to Russia.During the period of the Cold War, the Alaskan region became a frontier area for the United States, becoming home to military facilities and warning systems.According to Col. Michael J. Forsyth, U.S. Army, the closeness of Russia and Alaska, only about ninety kilometres apart across the Bering Strait, meant that this region became highly significant to the United States' defence plans.From today's point of view, the strategic location of Alaska makes the state very important to the policies of the U.S. related to the Arctic, energy security, and even environmental policies.Thinking back, what seems clear to us now is that the Russians sold Alaska due to immediate needs rather than future considerations. In order to solve the problem, they lost a valuable resource for Russia.Conclusively, the Alaska Purchase should not have been done as it has had a significant impact that will remain throughout history.
Article Summary: Russia sold Alaska to the U.S. in 1867 for only $7,200,000. The sale was based on economic and political reasons. However, the region proved immensely valuable both strategically and naturally. Alaska is home to some of the world's most significant undeveloped mineral deposits. The Prudhoe Bay oil field was discovered in 1968.

Article Title: AI data centers are causing 'stress' not just to tech companies, but also private insurers
Article Text:
Massive investments, growing risks



Unique challenges for data centre insurance companies





AI data centers are reportedly putting new pressure on the insurance industry. According to a CNBC report, experts warn that the rapid growth of these projects is becoming a “stress test” not just for tech companies, but also for private insurers and lenders. Consulting firm McKinsey estimates that global spending on data centers could reach $7 trillion by 2030. As costs rise, tech giants are increasingly relying on private equity, private credit and debt to fund these projects. The scale of investments is creating challenges for insurers.“When you put $10 to $20 billion plus in a single location, it creates capacity issues in the marketplace,” said Tom Harper, data center leader at insurance broker Gallagher as quoted in the CNBC report.He added that the sector has been a “real stress test” over the last few years, as insurers struggle to provide coverage for such large and complex projects. While these facilities are seen as high-quality assets, Harper said insuring them has become difficult due to their size and risk concentration.Private data center deals have crossed $10 billion regularly, with some reaching as high as $40 billion. Companies including Nvidia, Microsoft and BlackRock have already taken part in large investment deals.Rajat Rana, partner at Quinn Emanuel Urquhart & Sullivan, described the scale as unprecedented. “We’re talking about trillions of dollars, and almost going back to the same cycle where there’s almost no transparency about the financing structures — the scale is astronomical,” he said. He added that the boom in AI data centers could be “the largest peacetime investment project in human history.”Experts say the way these projects are financed is adding another layer of risk. Much of the funding is happening through complex and less transparent debt structures. Rana warned that this trend feels like “deja vu,” referring to past financial cycles. He said the lack of transparency could create risks for investors, insurers and pension funds.As stated in the CNBC report, data centers offer unique challenges due to their mix of real estate and advanced technology. Insurers are now designing custom policies to manage these risks. However, challenges remain. Large facilities are often located in areas prone to extreme weather, and they store expensive equipment, sometimes even before installation.Another key concern is the mismatch between the lifespan of data centers and the hardware they use. While data centers can last decades, GPUs — the chips powering AI — typically last around seven years. Rana described this as a “GPU debt treadmill,” saying, “This is almost like a treadmill that these AI data centers are running on.”He explained that companies may need to keep raising debt to upgrade infrastructure as technology evolves.
Article Summary: Private data center deals have crossed $10 billion regularly, with some reaching as high as $40 billion. McKinsey estimates that global spending on data centers could reach $7 trillion by 2030. Tech giants are increasingly relying on private equity, private credit and debt to fund these projects.

Article Title: Fugitive drug kingpin Virender Singh Basoya extradited from UAE in multi-crore cocaine bust
Article Text:
India's Narcotics Control Bureau has secured the extradition of Virender Singh Basoya from the UAE.





NEW DELHI: In a major breakthrough in the crackdown on international drug networks, the Narcotics Control Bureau (NCB) has secured the return of fugitive drug kingpin Virender Singh Basoya from the United Arab Emirates (UAE).Basoya, accused of orchestrating a massive multi-crore cocaine syndicate, was brought back to face trial following sustained inter-agency coordination and international legal action.Union Home minister Amit Shah confirmed the development. In a post on X, he said: "Modi govt is relentlessly tracking down drug traffickers hiding abroad and destroying their entire ecosystem with a ruthless approach. Creating a new milestone in the policy of zero tolerance against narcotics, the NCB secured the return of fugitive drug kingpin Virender Singh Basoya from the UAE.""By tracing the criminal through a top-to-bottom and bottom-to-top approach, our agencies have once again proven that no matter where drug traffickers hide, they cannot escape the long arm of Indian law," he said.The arrest marks a significant milestone in the Union government’s zero-tolerance policy against narcotics and international drug trafficking networks operating across borders.Basoya emerged as a key mastermind following one of the largest drug seizures in recent history, involving cocaine shipments valued in excess of ₹5,000 crore.As law enforcement agencies closed in on the syndicate's distribution networks, Basoya fled the country to evade arrest.Following detailed investigative trails, a Delhi court had previously issued a Non-Bailable Warrant (NBW) against him, enabling Indian agencies to initiate red notices and pursue extradition proceedings through diplomatic and international policing channels in the UAE.Officials stated that the operation relied on a dual "top-to-bottom and bottom-to-top" investigative framework. By mapping local street distribution networks upward while simultaneously intercepting high-level financial and logistical chains, the NCB successfully pinpointed Basoya’s foreign hideout.Senior law enforcement officials highlighted that the successful extradition sends a firm signal to fugitives attempting to seek refuge overseas:Basoya has been taken into NCB custody and will be presented before a specialized court in New Delhi.Investigators plan to interrogate him regarding international supply routes, financial money-laundering channels, and local accomplices linked to the multi-crore drug cartel. Further custodial disclosures are expected to assist in dismantling remaining nodes of the syndicate.
Article Summary: Virender Singh Basoya is accused of orchestrating a massive multi-crore cocaine syndicate. Basoya emerged as a key mastermind following one of the largest drug seizures in recent history. The arrest marks a significant milestone in the Union government’s zero-tolerance policy.

Article Title: Delhi traffic restrictions on Independence Day: Check key road closures, bus diversions for Aug 15
Article Text:
Delhi police conduct vehicle checking at the Aya Nagar Border as security arrangements intensify across national capital ahead of Independence Day , in New Delhi on Thursday.





NEW DELHI: The Delhi Traffic Police has issued a detailed traffic advisory ahead of the Independence Day celebrations at the Red Fort on August 15, with several roads to remain closed to general traffic and restrictions on buses and commercial vehicles.The restrictions will be in place primarily from 4am to 10am on August 15 for security and traffic management around the Red Fort. Only vehicles carrying valid parking labels will be permitted on several restricted stretches.Among the major roads that may be avoided during the restricted hours are Netaji Subhash Marg from Delhi Gate to Chatta Rail Chowk, Lothian Road between GPO Delhi and Chatta Rail Chowk, SP Mukherjee Marg between HC Sen Marg and Yamuna Bazar Chowk, Chandni Chowk Road from Fountain Chowk to Red Fort and Ring Road between Rajghat and ISBT.The traffic police has suggested alternative routes for motorists travelling between north and south Delhi. One route is via Aurobindo Marg, Safdarjung Road, Kamal Ataturk Marg, Kautilya Marg, Sardar Patel Marg, 11 Murti, Mother Teresa Crescent, Park Street, Mandir Marg, Panchkuian Road and Rani Jhansi Road. Another route is through Connaught Place, Minto Road, Bhavbhuti Marg, Ajmeri Gate, Shradhanand Marg, Lahori Gate Chowk, Naya Bazar and SP Mukherjee Marg.Traffic restrictions will also affect city and interstate buses. Buses bound for Kauria Pul, Red Fort and Old Delhi Railway Station will be diverted through the ISBT Bridge and will terminate at Boulevard Road near the Mori Gate U-turn. Buses heading towards New Delhi, Connaught Place and Central Secretariat will use the ISBT Bridge, Boulevard Road, Rani Jhansi Flyover, Rani Jhansi Road and Mandir Marg.Buses travelling towards South Delhi from the ISBT side will follow the diverted route up to Mandir Marg before proceeding through Shankar Road, Upper Ridge Road, Simon Bolivar Marg and Dhaula Kuan.Several buses normally terminating at Old Delhi Railway Station, Red Fort, Jama Masjid and Kauria Pul will be curtailed or diverted. Buses coming from Roshanara Road towards Old Delhi Railway Station will terminate opposite the State Bank of India inside Tis Hazari Court, while buses from Old Rohtak Road towards Old Delhi Railway Station and Red Fort will terminate at Mori Gate.The advisory also states that all private and mini buses will terminate at the MCD car parking area at Mori Gate. Gokhale Road will operate one-way from Mori Gate towards Kashmiri Gate and the Gokhale Market 'T' Point.Restrictions on commercial transport and interstate buses will also be enforced. Goods vehicles will not be permitted between Nizamuddin Khatta and Wazirabad Bridge from midnight on August 14 until 11am on August 15. Interstate buses will not be allowed between Maharana Pratap ISBT and Sarai Kale Khan ISBT during the same period.Local city buses, including DTC buses, will also face restrictions on the Ring Road between ISBT Kashmiri Gate and the NH-24/NH-9 junction at Nizamuddin Khatta from midnight on August 14 until 11am on August 15. Several other roads, including Lothian Road, Netaji Subhash Marg, SP Mukherjee Marg, parts of Ring Road, Mathura Road and Vikas Marg, will also be closed to inter-city and DTC buses during this period.Normal bus services are expected to resume after 11am on August 15. The traffic police has advised commuters to leave early to avoid last-minute congestion and inconvenience.The advisory also lists restrictions for pedestrians and visitors attending the Independence Day ceremony. The public has been advised not to carry cameras, binoculars, remote-control car keys, umbrellas, handbags, briefcases, transistors, cigarette lighters, tiffin or lunch boxes and water bottles. People have also been asked not to touch suspicious objects and to immediately alert the nearest police officer about any suspicious movement or unidentified object.The flying of paragliders, paramotors, hang gliders, UAVs, microlight aircraft, remotely piloted aircraft, hot-air balloons, quadcopters and similar aerial platforms has also been prohibited over Delhi during the specified security period.For commuters travelling to important locations, the advisory provides separate routes to Old Delhi Railway Station, New Delhi Railway Station and ISBT Kashmere Gate from different parts of the city.The Delhi Traffic Police has also arranged DTC recovery vans from 5am on August 15 until the diversions are cleared at Gokhale Marg, Ghata Masjid, Yamuna Bazar, Delhi Gate and Chatta Rail Chowk.Commuters have been advised to plan their journeys in advance and use the suggested alternative routes during the Independence Day traffic restrictions.
Article Summary: Several roads to remain closed to general traffic and restrictions on buses and commercial vehicles. Restrictions will be in place primarily from 4am to 10am on August 15 for security and traffic management around the Red Fort. Only vehicles carrying valid parking labels will be permitted on several restricted stretches.
